records.note: 'All healthcare payments collapse' names no payer, program or observable threshold; the consequence is a truism.
'Make it to a patient' names no clearance, coverage policy or adoption measure; the antecedent of 'it' is research generally.
'More coming every day' names no trial or readout; the accessibility half is his own shop, Fermata.
'Devices will matter' is a career thesis; no device, authorization, coverage policy or count can be written.
'Hard to blow up' and 'causing a ruckus' state no rule, filing or market threshold for PBMs; registry holds no PBM event.
Restated chart projection of antidepressant spending; no series, threshold or period. E-0049 is prescription volume, a different asset.
'A huge fight with health plans about their PBMs' names no rule, suit or agency action that could resolve.
'Already here and getting better every day' is a trend claim with no device, authorization or installed-base measure.
'More is coming' over four device-indication pairs; no sponsor named and no registry event for tFUS anxiety or nVNS PTSD authorization.
'These treatments' is a mixed device list, some already cleared; 'coming' states no clearance, coverage or adoption criterion.
'Psychedelic medicines are coming' is the class arrival reading of E-0024. 'Are coming' gives bin A; 'coming' is no deadline.
'For some period of time' with durability declared unknown; no trial, endpoint or threshold can be written.
Comparative with no benchmark: 'prove superior' names no head-to-head trial, endpoint or margin.
'The future is so close' and 'suffering less' are slogans; no approval, coverage or adoption measure.
'Huge impact in the future' over three findings; no endpoint, guideline or uptake measure can be written.
'More data is forthcoming' names no trial, endpoint or direction; E-0065 is one named Phase 3 trial the quote does not identify.
'Harder to deny' is not a coverage decision and names no plan; registry TMS coverage events are for accelerated or adolescent TMS.
'More to come' names no trial, indication or endpoint; the cited GLP-1 trials sit outside psychiatry.
'That price is going to go up' names no drug, series or period; no registry event holds drug prices.
Restatement with 'forever'; no named price series, threshold or period. 'Forever' is not a deadline.
'Nothing New and Good' has no countable set; no NTAP decision, device or date can be written.
Conditional on an unwritten payment path; 'new technology to the market' names no device or authorization.
No call on passage of the Breakthrough Therapies Act or H.R.1691; 'go a long way' has no criterion.
'The behavior will continue' across the industry; no company, case or count of enforcement actions is named.
Four unspecified changes in physician exposure to pharma marketing; no society, rule or measure, and 'tomorrow' is figurative.
Conditional and doubly hedged; 'potent intervention' names no ketosis trial, endpoint or effect size.
'No law so invasive' has no countable set; no bill, state or date, and the subject is not a psychiatric treatment decision.
An article title stating a stance; 'won't save us' names no board, action or measurable outcome.
Average creator earnings on fan-funded platforms; not a drug, device, payer or practice outcome in psychiatry.
'Someone is going to get F-d' names no party, payment or observable event.
'A more hot topic' is attention, not a coverage decision; no Part D policy change or date is asserted.
'Pressure on federal budgets and premiums' names no series, threshold or plan year.
'Harsh awakening' and 'not going to cut it' name no company event, rate or payer policy; conditional on an unwritten change.
Comparative with no benchmark: 'not that much better' contracts, with no rate, code or published policy.
'A couple of exits' over an undefined set of companies, and 'not gonna change healthcare' has no measure.
'Therapists are going to quit' names no platform, workforce series or threshold.
'Until it's not' names no company, date or observable failure.
'The opportunity is coming' names no payer, at-risk program or contract; the registry holds no value-based care event.
A perceived shift toward value-based care; no payer, program or series that could count it.
'Lead to improvement in mental health care' is a generic closing claim with no measure.
Comparative with no benchmark: 'even more anti-trans than Texas' names no rule, order or agency action.
